claim: Passing build and API checks does not guarantee a UI is correct — visual regressions like clipped labels can still slip through and only surface in visual QA (e.g., screenshot review). There is unresolved tension over who owns catching and being accountable for these issues: engineering treats build/API-green as 'done,' while visual QA is described as the designer's responsibility.
revalidate_when: Team explicitly agrees on visual QA ownership and gating criteria for 'done'
Screenshot/visual regression checks are added to the automated build or API gate
tension_between: Build and API checks passing means the chart page task is complete
Visual QA (owned by the designer) is a separate, required check that can fail even when build/API checks pass

revalidate_when: source, error details, date, and affected scope for the provider-broken claim are provided

claim: A terminal transcript captured during deployment debugging contained an exposed private token; must be redacted/rotated before the transcript is stored or shared, and raw secrets should never be persisted in memory.
revalidate_when: token has been rotated and transcript redacted
original incident evidence is available for re-review
a canonical note is created or edited to explicitly confirm the relationship between the two notes
ownership of UI visual QA approval is explicitly clarified or reconciled by a decision-maker
tension_between: new note: backend agents can approve UI appearance
active memory: designer owns visual QA

claim: User stated a standing preference that applies broadly across future tasks; it should be surfaced cheaply at the start of every session rather than rediscovered each time.
revalidate_when: original incident details/evidence become available for verification
user contradicts or updates this preference in a later session

claim: A UI table appeared correct but was showing stale data because the server-side cache was not being invalidated properly; fixing cache invalidation logic resolved the stale display.
revalidate_when: similar stale-data symptom reappears in another UI view backed by server-side caching

claim: For visual QA tasks in this project, prefer the project's visual QA harness over ad hoc live browser tool sessions — the harness produces reusable artifacts, whereas manual browser driving does not.
revalidate_when: next time an agent performs visual QA or browser-based verification work

claim: A pricing decision saved last month may now be outdated because the provider changed its pricing this week; needs revalidation before being relied on again.
revalidate_when: original pricing decision is re-checked against new rates

claim: User prefers expensive/premium models be reserved for a few specific high-value use cases, with routine work handled by cheaper/standard models.
revalidate_when: user redefines which use cases count as premium
cost/performance tradeoffs of available models change significantly
specific prior decisions and their content are identified with citable evidence
